verses.zh: 有法利赛人和几个文士从耶路撒冷来，到耶稣那里聚集。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] the Pharisees[NOTE:2] and some of the experts in the law[NOTE:3] who came from Jerusalem[NOTE:4] gathered around him.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
See the note on Pharisees in 2:16.
Or “and some of the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 1:22.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 他们曾看见他的门徒中有人用俗手，就是没有洗的手，吃饭。
verses.en: And they saw that some of Jesus’ disciples[NOTE:1] ate their bread with unclean hands, that is, unwashed.
notes: Grk “his disciples.”

verses.zh: （原来法利赛人和犹太人都拘守古人的遗传，若不仔细洗手就不吃饭；
verses.en: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they perform a ritual washing,[NOTE:1] holding fast to the tradition of the elders.
notes: Grk “except they wash the hands with a fist,” a ceremonial washing (though the actual method is uncertain).

verses.zh: 从市上来，若不洗浴也不吃饭；还有好些别的规矩，他们历代拘守，就是洗杯、罐、铜器等物。）
verses.en: And when they come from the marketplace,[NOTE:1] they do not eat unless they wash. They hold fast to many other traditions: the washing of cups, pots, kettles, and dining couches.[NOTE:2])[NOTE:3]
notes: See the note on marketplaces in Mark 6:56.

Several significant witnesses (P45vid א B L Δ 28*) lack “and dining couches” (καὶ κλινῶν, kai klinōn), while the majority of mss (A D W Θ ƒ1,13 33 M latt) have the reading. Although normally the shorter reading is to be preferred, especially when it is backed by excellent witnesses as in this case, there are some good reasons to consider καὶ κλινῶν as authentic: (1) Although the addition of κλινῶν could be seen as motivated by a general assimilation to the purity regulations in Lev 15 (as some have argued), there are three problems with such a supposition: (a) the word κλίνη (klinē) does not occur in the LXX of Lev 15; (b) nowhere in Lev 15 is the furniture washed or sprinkled; and (c) the context of Lev 15 is about sexual impurity, while the most recent evidence suggests that κλίνη in Mark 7:4, in keeping with the other terms used here, refers to a dining couch (cf. BDAG 549 s.v. κλίνη 2). Thus, it is difficult to see καὶ κλινῶν as a motivated reading. (2) κλίνη, though a relatively rare term in the NT, is in keeping with Markan usage (cf. Mark 4:21; 7:30). (3) The phrase could have been dropped accidentally, at least in some cases, via homoioteleuton. (4) The phrase may have been deliberately expunged by some scribes who thought the imagery of washing a dining couch quite odd. The longer reading, in this case, can thus be argued as the harder reading. On balance, even though a decision is difficult (especially because of the weighty external evidence for the shorter reading), it is preferable to retain καὶ κλινῶν in the text.
Verses 3-4 represent parenthetical remarks by the author, giving background information.

verses.zh: 法利赛人和文士问他说：「你的门徒为甚么不照古人的遗传，用俗手吃饭呢？」
verses.en: The Pharisees and the experts in the law asked him, “Why do your disciples not live according to the tradition of the elders, but eat[NOTE:1] with unwashed hands?”
notes: Grk “eat bread.”

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「以赛亚指着你们假冒为善之人所说的预言是不错的。如经上说：这百姓用嘴唇尊敬我，心却远离我。
verses.en: He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written:“‘This people honors me with their lips,but their hearts[NOTE:1] are far from me.
notes: The term “heart” is a collective singular in the Greek text.

verses.zh: 他们将人的吩咐当作道理教导人，所以拜我也是枉然。
verses.en: They worship me in vain,teaching as doctrine the commandments of men.’[NOTE:1]
notes: A quotation from Isa 29:13.

verses.zh: 你们是离弃　神的诫命，拘守人的遗传」；
verses.en: Having no regard[NOTE:1] for the command of God, you hold fast to human tradition.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Having left the command.”

The majority of mss, mostly Byzantine ([A] ƒ13 33 M), have at the end of v. 8 material that seems to have come from v. 4 and v. 13: “the washing of pots and cups, and you do many other similar things.” A slight variation on the wording occurs at the very beginning of v. 8 in mostly Western witnesses (D Θ 0131vid 28 565 it). Such floating texts are usually signs of scribal emendations. The fact that the earliest and most reliable mss, as well as other significant witnesses (P45 א B L W Δ 0274 ƒ1 co), lacked this material also strongly suggests that the longer reading is secondary.

verses.zh: 又说：「你们诚然是废弃　神的诫命，要守自己的遗传。
verses.en: He also said to them, “You neatly reject the commandment of God in order to set up[NOTE:1] your tradition.
notes: The translation here follows the reading στήσητε (stēsēte, “set up”) found in D W Θ ƒ1 28 565 2542 it sys,p Cyp. The majority of mss here read τηρήσητε (tērēsete; א A L ƒ13 33 M co) or τηρῆτε (tērēte; B), both translated “keep.” It is hard to know which reading is best: On the one hand, τηρήσητε/τηρῆτε has much stronger external support, but στήσητε is a more difficult reading. What makes “keep” suspect is that it appears in two different forms, suggesting independent alterations of a difficult reading. Further, scribes may have been influenced by the preceding “commandment of God” to change the text toward “keep” (TCGNT 81), a common enough expression (cf. Matt 19:17; John 14:15; 1 Tim 6:1; 1 John 5:3; Rev 14:12). Thus, the more difficult reading is “set up.” Also, the more natural opposite of “reject” (ἀθεῖτε [atheite], literally “you set aside”) is “set up.” However, the Western reading may have been influenced by Exod 6:4 or Heb 10:9, but this likelihood seems remote. Thus, “set up” is more likely to be the earlier reading here.

verses.zh: 摩西说：『当孝敬父母』；又说：『咒骂父母的，必治死他。』
verses.en: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’[NOTE:1] and, ‘Whoever insults his father or mother must be put to death.’[NOTE:2]
notes: A quotation from Exod 20:12; Deut 5:16.
A quotation from Exod 21:17; Lev 20:9.

verses.zh: 你们倒说：『人若对父母说：我所当奉给你的，已经作了各耳板』（各耳板就是供献的意思），
verses.en: But you say that if anyone tells his father or mother, ‘Whatever help you would have received from me is corban’[NOTE:1] (that is, a gift for God),
notes: Corban is a Hebrew loanword (transliterated in the Greek text and in most modern English translations) referring to something that has been set aside as a gift to be given to God at some later date, but which is still in the possession of the owner (L&N 53.22). According to contemporary Jewish tradition the person who made this claim was absolved from responsibility to support or assist his parents, a clear violation of the Mosaic law to honor one’s parents (v. 10).

verses.zh: 以后你们就不容他再奉养父母。
verses.en: then you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or mother.

verses.zh: 这就是你们承接遗传，废了　神的道。你们还做许多这样的事。」
verses.en: Thus you nullify[NOTE:1] the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many things like this.”
notes: Grk “nullifying.” This participle shows the results of the Pharisees’ command.

verses.zh: 耶稣又叫众人来，对他们说：「你们都要听我的话，也要明白。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he called the crowd again and said to them, “Listen to me, everyone, and understand.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 从外面进去的不能污秽人，惟有从里面出来的乃能污秽人。」（有古卷加：
verses.en: There is nothing outside of a person that can defile him by going into him. Rather, it is what comes out of a person that defiles him.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Most later mss add 7:16 “Let anyone with ears to hear, listen.” This verse is included in A D W Θ ƒ1,13 33 M latt sy, but is lacking in significant Alexandrian mss and a few others (א B L Δ* 0274 28). It appears to be a scribal gloss (see 4:9 and 4:23), perhaps introduced as a reiteration of the thought in 7:14, and is almost certainly not an original part of the Greek text of Mark. The present translation follows NA28 in omitting the verse number, a procedure also followed by a number of other modern translations.

verses.zh: 有耳可听的，就应当听！）
耶稣离开众人，进了屋子，门徒就问他这比喻的意思。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when Jesus[NOTE:2] had left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about the parable.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「你们也是这样不明白吗？岂不晓得凡从外面进入的，不能污秽人，
verses.en: He said to them, “Are you so foolish? Don’t you understand that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him?

verses.zh: 因为不是入他的心，乃是入他的肚腹，又落到茅厕里。（这是说，各样的食物都是洁净的）」；
verses.en: For it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and then goes out into the sewer.”[NOTE:1] (This means all foods are clean.)[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “into the latrine.”
This is a parenthetical note by the author.

verses.zh: 又说：「从人里面出来的，那才能污秽人；
verses.en: He said, “What comes out of a person defiles him.

verses.zh: 因为从里面，就是从人心里，发出恶念、苟合、
verses.en: For from within, out of the human heart, come evil ideas, sexual immorality, theft, murder,

verses.zh: 偷盗、凶杀、奸淫、贪婪、邪恶、诡诈、淫荡、嫉妒、谤讟、骄傲、狂妄。
verses.en: adultery, greed, evil, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, pride, and folly.

verses.zh: 这一切的恶都是从里面出来，且能污秽人。」
verses.en: All these evils come from within and defile a person.”

verses.zh: 耶稣从那里起身，往泰尔、西顿的境内去，进了一家，不愿意人知道，却隐藏不住。
verses.en: After Jesus[NOTE:1] left there, he went to the region of Tyre.[NOTE:2] When he went into a house, he did not want anyone to know, but[NOTE:3] he was not able to escape notice.
notes: Grk “He”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.tc Most mss, including early and significant witnesses (א A B ƒ1,13 33 M lat), have here καὶ Σιδῶνος (kai Sidōnos, “and Sidon”). The Western text, as well as several other significant mss (D L W Δ Θ 28 565 it), lack the words. Although the external evidence is on the side of inclusion, it is difficult to explain why scribes would omit the mention of Sidon. On the other hand, the parallels in v. 31 and Matt 15:21 would be sufficient motivation for scribes to add Sidon here. Furthermore, every other mention of Tyre in the Gospels is accompanied by Sidon, putting pressure on scribes to conform this text as well. The shorter reading therefore, though without compelling external evidence on its side, is strongly supported by internal evidence, rendering judgment on its authenticity fairly certain.
Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 当下，有一个妇人，她的小女儿被污鬼附着，听见耶稣的事，就来俯伏在他脚前。
verses.en: Instead, a woman whose young daughter had an unclean spirit[NOTE:1] immediately heard about him and came and fell at his feet.
notes: Unclean spirit refers to an evil spirit.

verses.zh: 这妇人是希腊人，属叙利腓尼基族。她求耶稣赶出那鬼离开她的女儿。
verses.en: The woman was a Greek, of Syrophoenician origin. She[NOTE:1] asked him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
notes: Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 耶稣对她说：「让儿女们先吃饱，不好拿儿女的饼丢给狗吃。」
verses.en: He said to her, “Let the children be satisfied first, for it is not right to take the children’s bread and to throw it to the dogs.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The term dogs does not refer to wild dogs (scavenging animals roaming around the countryside) in this context, but to small dogs taken in as house pets. It is thus not a derogatory term per se, but is instead intended by Jesus to indicate the privileged position of the Jews (especially his disciples) as the initial recipients of Jesus’ ministry. The woman’s response of faith and her willingness to accept whatever Jesus would offer pleased him to such an extent that he granted her request. This is the only miracle mentioned in Mark that Jesus performed at a distance without ever having seen the afflicted person, or issuing some sort of audible command.tn Or “lap dogs, house dogs,” as opposed to dogs on the street. The diminutive form originally referred to puppies or little dogs, then to house pets. In some Hellenistic uses κυνάριον (kunarion) simply means “dog.”

verses.zh: 妇人回答说：「主啊，不错；但是狗在桌子底下也吃孩子们的碎渣儿。」
verses.en: She answered, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”

verses.zh: 耶稣对她说：「因这句话，你回去吧；鬼已经离开你的女儿了。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he said to her, “Because you said this, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 她就回家去，见小孩子躺在床上，鬼已经出去了。
verses.en: She went home and found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone.

verses.zh: 耶稣又离了泰尔的境界，经过西顿，就从低加坡里境内来到加利利海。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] went out again from the region of Tyre[NOTE:3] and came through Sidon[NOTE:4] to the Sea of Galilee in the region of the Decapolis.[NOTE:5]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.
For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

The Decapolis refers to a group of towns (originally consisting of ten; the Greek name literally means “ten towns”) whose region (except for Scythopolis) lay on the east side of the Jordan River. Although frequently seen as a league of independent city states organized by the Roman general Pompey, contemporary sources do not support such a view. Rather their unity came from their Greek (Hellenistic) culture and religions, which set them apart from surrounding areas.

verses.zh: 有人带着一个耳聋舌结的人来见耶稣，求他按手在他身上。
verses.en: They brought to him a deaf man who had difficulty speaking, and they asked him to place his hands on him.

verses.zh: 耶稣领他离开众人，到一边去，就用指头探他的耳朵，吐唾沫抹他的舌头，
verses.en: After Jesus[NOTE:1] took him aside privately, away from the crowd, he put his fingers in the man’s[NOTE:2] ears, and after spitting, he touched his tongue.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “his”; the referent (the deaf man) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

After spitting, he touched his tongue. It was not uncommon in Judaism of the day to associate curative powers with a person’s saliva. The scene as a whole reflects Jesus’ willingness to get close to people and have physical contact with them where appropriate. See W. L. Lane, Mark (NICNT), 267 n. 78.

verses.zh: 望天叹息，对他说：「以法大！」就是说：「开了吧！」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he looked up to heaven and said with a sigh, “Ephphatha” (that is, “Be opened”).[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
The author’s parenthetical note gives the meaning of the Aramaic word Ephphatha.

verses.zh: 他的耳朵就开了，舌结也解了，说话也清楚了。
verses.en: And immediately the man’s[NOTE:1] ears were opened, his tongue loosened, and he spoke plainly.
notes: Grk “his”; the referent (the man who had been a deaf mute) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶稣嘱咐他们不要告诉人；但他越发嘱咐，他们越发传扬开了。
verses.en: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But as much as he ordered them not to do this, they proclaimed it all the more.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “but as much as he ordered them, these rather so much more proclaimed.” Greek tends to omit direct objects when they are clear from the context, but these usually need to be supplied for the modern English reader. Here what Jesus ordered has been clarified (“ordered them not to do this”), and the pronoun “it” has been supplied after “proclaimed.”

verses.zh: 众人分外希奇，说：「他所做的事都好，他连聋子也叫他们听见，哑巴也叫他们说话。」
verses.en: People were completely astounded and said, “He has done everything well. He even makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.”
